public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 42: Maximal Sidon Sets and Disjoint Difference Sets

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/42](https://www.erdosproblems.com/42)

This problem asks whether maximal Sidon sets can coexist with other Sidon sets that have
disjoint difference sets (apart from 0).
-/

@[expose] public section

open Function Set Filter
open scoped Pointwise

namespace Erdos42

/--
**Erdős Problem 42**: Let M ≥ 1 and N be sufficiently large in terms of M. Is it true that for every
maximal Sidon set `A ⊆ {1,…,N}` there is another Sidon set `B ⊆ {1,…,N}` of size M such that
`(A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0}`?

This was proved for all $M$ by GPT 5.5 Pro (prompted by Sandhu), see discussion thread for more details.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Shashi456/erdos-formalizations/blob/main/Erdos/P42/CompactCayley/Proof.lean"]
theorem erdos_42 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ M ≥ 1, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (_ : IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N),
    ∃ᵉ (B : Set ℕ), B ⊆ Set.Icc 1 N ∧ IsSidon B ∧ B.ncard = M ∧
    ((A - A) ∩ (B - B)) = {0} := by
  sorry

/--
A variant asking for explicit bounds on how large N needs to be in terms of M.

This version provides a constructive function f such that for all M ≥ 1 and N ≥ f(M),
every maximal Sidon set A ⊆ {1,…,N} has another Sidon set B ⊆ {1,…,N} of size M with
disjoint difference sets (apart from 0).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11,
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/KitaKen1/erdos-42-constructive-variant/blob/1f82c76be43cb56f22e2f7f792e392d5fb3ff78c/lean/Erdos42Constructive.lean"]
theorem erdos_42.variants.constructive : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ (f : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ (M N : ℕ) (_ : 1 ≤ M) (_ : f M ≤ N),
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (_ : IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N), ∃ᵉ (B : Set ℕ),
      B ⊆ Set.Icc 1 N ∧ IsSidon B ∧ B.ncard = M ∧
      ((A - A) ∩ (B - B)) = {0} := by
  sorry


/-  ## Related results and examples -/

/--
The set `{1, 2, 4}` is a maximal Sidon set in `{1, ..., 4}`.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 11]
theorem example_maximal_sidon : IsMaximalSidonSetIn {1, 2, 4} 4 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro x hx
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> simp [Set.mem_Icc]
  · intro i₁ hi₁ j₁ hj₁ i₂ hi₂ j₂ hj₂ hsum
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hi₁ hj₁ hi₂ hj₂
    rcases hi₁ with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases hj₁ with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases hi₂ with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases hj₂ with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    simp_all
  · intro x hx hxA
    simp only [Set.mem_Icc] at hx; obtain ⟨hx1, hx2⟩ := hx
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff, not_or] at hxA
    obtain ⟨hne1, hne2, hne4⟩ := hxA
    have hx3 : x = 3 := (by omega); subst hx3
    intro hbad
    have := hbad 1 (by simp) 2 (by simp) 3 (by simp) 2 (by simp) (by norm_num)
    rcases this with ⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩ <;> omega

/--
The difference set of `{1, 2, 4}` is `{0, 1, 2, 3}`.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 11]
theorem example_difference_set : ({1, 2, 4} : Set ℕ) - {1, 2, 4} = {0, 1, 2, 3} := by
  ext x
  simp only [Set.mem_sub, Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨a, ha, b, hb, rfl⟩
    rcases ha with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases hb with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    simp
  · rintro (rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl)
    · exact ⟨1, by decide, 1, by decide, by decide⟩
    · exact ⟨2, by decide, 1, by decide, by decide⟩
    · exact ⟨4, by decide, 2, by decide, by decide⟩
    · exact ⟨4, by decide, 1, by decide, by decide⟩

/--
For any maximal Sidon set, the difference set contains 0.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 11]
theorem maximal_sidon_contains_zero (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (hA : IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N) : 0 ∈ A - A := by
  obtain ⟨hAsub, hAsidon, hAmax⟩ := hA
  have hne : A.Nonempty
  · by_contra hemp; rw [Set.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty] at hemp
    exact hAmax (Set.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨le_refl 1, hN⟩)
      (by rw [hemp]; exact id) (by
        rw [hemp, Set.empty_union]
        exact fun _ hi _ hj _ hk _ hl _ => by
          simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hi hj hk hl
          subst hi
          subst hj
          subst hk
          subst hl
          exact Or.inl ⟨rfl, rfl⟩)
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
  have := Set.sub_mem_sub ha ha
  rwa [Nat.sub_self] at this

end Erdos42

findings.description: The docstring presents this as "A variant asking for explicit bounds on how large N needs to be in terms of M" that "provides a constructive function f". The Lean right-hand side is `∃ (f : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ M N, 1 ≤ M → f M ≤ N → ∀ A, IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N → ∃ B ...`. That is a classical existence statement with no explicitness or computability requirement. It is exactly the Skolemization of `∀ M ≥ 1, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, ...`, so it is logically equivalent to the RHS of `erdos_42`. I proved this `↔` in a scratch file (`variant_iff_main`, only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound): (⇒) take the threshold f M; (⇐) pick a threshold for each M by choice. So the declaration adds nothing to `erdos_42`. Yet it has its own `research solved` and `formal_proof` records, which suggest that explicit bounds have been formalized. The linked proof disclaims this itself: "This is an existence proof. It does not compute an explicit numerical bound." and "The current statement asks only for existence of a threshold function. It follows from the solved main theorem by classical choice." The Lean statement is true and non-vacuous, but it does not state the explicit-bound claim its docstring and name describe.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/42 (LaTeX source, last edited 10 May 2026) poses only the qualitative question. Its quantitative remark reads: "This was proved for all $M$ by GPT 5.5 Pro (prompted by Sandhu); discussion of the proof is ongoing in the comments, but it seems that it can prove, for example, that there exists such a $B$ with $|B| \gg (\log\log N/\log\log\log N)^{1/2}$." In the forum, T. Bloom (29 Apr 2026) wrote: "It would be good to write down a quantitatively effective version of the key lemma to see how large N needs to be in terms of M". K. Barreto (29 Apr 2026) claims "an effective bound $N_0(M)\leq\exp(\exp(CM^2\log(2M)))$". The linked proof, KitaKen1/erdos-42-constructive-variant (lean/Erdos42Constructive.lean), says it proves only the threshold-existence form, by classical choice from the main theorem.
findings.suggested_fix: Option 1: re-document the variant honestly, e.g. "Skolemized form of `erdos_42`: there is a threshold function f with …; equivalent to `erdos_42` by choice; no explicit bound", or drop it as redundant. Option 2: state a genuinely explicit bound, with a category matching its status. Example: `∃ C > (0:ℝ), ∀ M ≥ 1, ∀ N : ℕ, Real.exp (Real.exp (C * M^2 * Real.log (2*M))) ≤ N → ∀ A, IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N → ∃ B ⊆ Set.Icc 1 N, IsSidon B ∧ B.ncard = M ∧ (A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0}`. Or the page's form: `∃ c > (0:ℝ), ∀ᶠ N in atTop, ∀ A, IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N → ∃ B ⊆ Set.Icc 1 N, IsSidon B ∧ c * √(Real.log (Real.log N) / Real.log (Real.log (Real.log N))) ≤ B.ncard ∧ (A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0}`.

reformulations.difference: The Lean quantifies only over inclusion-maximal Sidon sets (`IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N`). The docstring matches this ("for every maximal Sidon set"). The current erdosproblems.com text says "for every Sidon set $A\subset\{1,\ldots,N\}$". The same RHS appears in `erdos_42.variants.constructive`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (⇐) Every maximal Sidon set is a Sidon set, and it is nonempty for N ≥ 1 (the file's `maximal_sidon_contains_zero`). (⇒) Take a nonempty Sidon A ⊆ [1,N]. Among the finitely many Sidon supersets of A inside [1,N], a maximal one A' exists, and A−A ⊆ A'−A'. So a B with (A'−A')∩(B−B)={0} also gives (A−A)∩(B−B)={0}; 0 lies in both difference sets because A and B are nonempty (M ≥ 1). The only exception is A=∅. For it the literal source wording is false, since (∅−∅)∩(B−B)=∅≠{0}, so the maximal form is the sensible reading. Tao on the forum (5 Dec 2025): "Without loss of generality one can take A to be a maximal Sidon set (this was the original form of the problem)." In a scratch file I proved `LeanRHS ↔ SourceRHS`, where SourceRHS ranges over all nonempty Sidon A ⊆ Icc 1 N, and `literal_source_false`, the refutation of the all-Sidon-sets version including ∅. Only standard axioms are used.

reformulations.difference: `A - A` and `B - B` are pointwise differences in `Set ℕ` with truncated subtraction. They hold only the non-negative differences (negative ones collapse to 0), not the integer difference sets of the source.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For nonempty A ⊆ ℕ, (A−A)_ℕ = (A−A)_ℤ ∩ ℕ. Also (A−A)_ℤ ∩ (B−B)_ℤ is symmetric under negation, so it equals {0} exactly when its non-negative part does. Nonemptiness holds here: A is maximal with N ≥ 1, and B.ncard = M ≥ 1. I proved `diff_nat_iff_int` in Lean: for nonempty A, B ⊆ ℕ, `(A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0}` in `Set ℕ` iff the corresponding identity holds for the integer images. It uses only propext and Quot.sound. The same applies to the variant.

review.notes:
The main statement `erdos_42` matches erdosproblems.com/42. The source says "every Sidon set" and the Lean restricts to maximal Sidon sets; both that difference and the truncated ℕ subtraction are proven equivalences (recorded under reformulations). `answer(True)` and `research solved` agree with the page ("This was proved for all M by GPT 5.5 Pro (prompted by Sandhu)") and with the Lean formalization discussed in the forum (Shashi456 Proof.lean, which targets exactly this statement shape; confirmed by N. Sothanaphan on 12 May 2026). The site labels the problem "SOLVED (LEAN)", i.e. "resolved in some other way than a proof or disproof", rather than PROVED. Its text still says the answer is yes for all M, and the repository has no finer category, so I do not count this as a status issue.

Minor metadata, not mathematics: the variant carries `formal_proof using formal_conjectures`. The attribute docs define that kind as "formally proved in this repository", but the link points to an external repository (KitaKen1/erdos-42-constructive-variant), so `lean4` seems the right kind.

The helper declarations `example_maximal_sidon`, `example_difference_set` and `maximal_sidon_contains_zero` are sorry-free and correct. The docstring of `example_difference_set` calls {0,1,2,3} "the difference set of {1,2,4}". That is the ℕ-truncated version; the integer difference set is {0,±1,±2,±3}. This is harmless.
